question.problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$
question.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have $u(x,y)=2x-y$ and $v(x,y)=x+2y.$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =-1 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
